items.title: George Avakian interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 21, 1998
items.q: I consider Nicholas to be the outstanding young jazz musician in the world today... and he is also the closest thing I’ve heard to say Clifford Brown.

ctx.x: I’m sorry, the younger white musicians?

The younger black musicians, did I say white? The younger black musicians don’t know the origins of jazz and they don’t know say the New Orleans tradition except for those who are down in New Orleans. A great example of the positive side of a young black musician knowing the foundation of the music is Nicholas Payton. I consider Nicholas to be the outstanding young jazz musician in the world today, by a considerable margin, and one reason is that he not only knows the music from the beginning on, but he can play…
goodness, and that was the duet album with Doc Cheatham and the performance of “Stardust.” I can’t even talk about it.
